deep.reconstruction:
This page contains no mathematics: no formulas, computations or derivations. It is a set of reading notes and excerpts, partly verbatim and partly paraphrased, from J. F. Herbart's 'Lehrbuch zur Einleitung in die Philosophie'. It continues the previous page's notes on Herbart's §§238-243 about logic and conceptual method. The next page continues with Einleitung §§207-211 and a reference to Herbart's 1822 essay on applying mathematics to psychology. The contents are:

(1) §244. Synthesis belongs to the 'third case' of the previous page: how new concepts are generated where old ones do not suffice. Herbart says he could not start with examples but had to point directly to the main points: the concepts of causality and of space. On causality, abstract concepts become useless once abstraction has removed the essential feature; in a system each concept to be generated has its place where it is found. The self-preservation of substances is found from the problems of inherence and change. The assumption of inner states would otherwise be derived only problematically and waveringly, but follows easily from the investigation of the spatial co-existence ('Zusammen') of substances. The new expressions (spatial relations, the doctrine of 'Reale' and their connections) are more remote consequences.

(2) Section headings: §246 (on the presentation), §247 (plan of the encyclopaedia), §248 'own systematics'.
- Practical philosophy and metaphysics are wholly disparate sciences. Logic stands in the same relation to both and to every other branch of learning.
- Each special method belongs where its problem arises. Thus the 'method of relations' (Methode der Beziehungen) belongs to metaphysics, because there the problems are given contradictions that are nonetheless empirical concepts of something real.
- Kant's transcendental logic is dismissed as a failed chapter of psychology.
- Practical philosophy is systematised from aesthetic judgments about relations of the will.
- The other parts of aesthetics cannot follow this model, since in them the simultaneous (harmony) and successive (melody) beautiful are differently weighted.
- Psychology cannot have its course of thought prescribed as strictly as metaphysics, so its systematic form will long waver.

(3) §249, history of philosophy. Then Cap. V, 'Of general metaphysics':
- §§203-205: method of relations; causality.
- §206: matter. The problem of matter cannot be treated by the method of relations alone, since space, time and motion claim to indicate something real. The true causal relation must first be known from inherence and causality.
- A merely spatial Real is absurd, because extendedness or juxtaposition is no predicate or quality of the Real. Every actual matter shows attraction or repulsion, pointing to a hidden inner causality.
- Matter also requires development and correction of the concept of space.

This is Herbart's architecture of metaphysics: methodology, ontology, synechology and eidolology. It is the philosophical background to Riemann's own Naturphilosophie fragments, whose Herbartian influence is well known (Riemann himself wrote 'Der Verfasser ist Herbartianer...').

results.what: Excerpts/paraphrase of Herbart, Lehrbuch zur Einleitung in die Philosophie, §§244-249 and Cap. V §§203-206 (synthesis of new concepts; causality and space; method of relations; matter requires inner causality and a corrected concept of space)

deep.surprise_reason: Pure reading notes on Herbart's philosophy. Riemann's study of Herbart is well documented and his Naturphilosophie fragments openly declare Herbartian influence. There is no mathematics and no original result.
transcription_corrections: Line 1: 'Herbart[?] ... nicht mit Beispielen beginnen' is more likely a phrase like 'Hier konnte man nicht mit Beispielen beginnen'. It is not the name Herbart.
'Nicht zu verdienen[?]' is probably 'Nicht zu verwundern'.
'die Benennung der inneren Zustände' is likely 'die Annahme der inneren Zustände'.
Final word of §244 '[-Raum-] zu stande' should be read 'Zustände'.
'Elasticität[?] Raum' in §206 is doubtful; the sense is a Real conceived as merely filling or spread in space ('im Raume verbreitet'), not 'elasticity'.
'Cap. V. Von der allgemeinen Metaphysik' and the §§203-206 refer to Herbart's Einleitung, not to Riemann's own numbering.
